title: What does the ISM say about cyber security awareness training?
description: What the September 2026 Information Security Manual says about cyber security awareness training, privileged user training, registers and social engineering.
shortAnswer: The Australian Signals Directorate's Information Security Manual (ISM) recommends that all personnel undertake cyber security awareness training annually (ISM-0252), that privileged users undertake tailored training annually (ISM-1565), and that organisations maintain a training register (ISM-2022). The Chief Information Security Officer oversees the program (ISM-0735). Further controls cover business email compromise, social engineering, synthetic impersonation and posting work information online.
keyTakeaways: As at September 2026, the current release is the Information security manual (September 2026), published by the Australian Signals Directorate (ASD) on cyber.gov.au.
Annual awareness training for all personnel (ISM-0252) must cover five topics, from security appointments to incident reporting.
Privileged users need tailored annual training (ISM-1565), and a training register must be maintained (ISM-2022).
Newer controls add role-based advice on business email compromise, help desk social engineering, and, from September 2026, verifying requests that could be synthetic voice or video (ISM-2126).
The ISM is a risk-based framework: it is mandatory for Commonwealth entities through the PSPF and widely adopted voluntarily elsewhere.
appliesTo: State, territory and local government bodies that adopt the ISM
Service providers and suppliers assessed against the ISM
Private organisations using the ISM as a security baseline

sections.heading: What is the ISM and who has to follow it?

blocks.text: The ISM is ASD's cyber security framework, which an organisation applies through its own risk management framework to protect information technology and operational technology systems. ASD publishes it on [cyber.gov.au](https://www.cyber.gov.au/business-government/asds-cyber-security-frameworks/ism) and updates it regularly; as at September 2026 the current release is the Information security manual (September 2026).

The ISM itself is written as guidance with security controls, not as legislation. Its force for Commonwealth entities comes from the [Protective Security Policy Framework](/regulations/pspf-security-awareness-training): PSPF Release 2026 requires a cyber security strategy and uplift plan to manage cyber security risks in accordance with the ISM. Other governments, suppliers and private organisations adopt it voluntarily or through contract.

Each control carries an applicability marking: NC (non-classified systems, government and non-government), OS (OFFICIAL: Sensitive), P (PROTECTED), S (SECRET) and TS (TOP SECRET). All of the awareness controls discussed on this page are marked for every level, NC through TS.

sections.heading: Which ISM controls require awareness training?

blocks.text: Four controls form the training core: three sit in the 'Cyber security awareness training' section of the Guidelines for personnel security, and ISM-0735 sits in the 'Chief information security officer' section of the Guidelines for cyber security roles. They are listed below with their revision details from the September 2026 release.

blocks.caption: Core ISM cyber security awareness training controls, Information security manual (September 2026)
head: Control
What it says
Revision and last update
rows: Cyber security awareness training is undertaken annually by all personnel and covers: its purpose; security appointments and contacts; authorised use of systems and their resources; protection of systems and their resources; and reporting of cyber security incidents and suspected compromises.

blocks.text: These controls sit under the ISM's cyber security principle PRO-14, which states that personnel are provided with ongoing cyber security awareness training, including operational security considerations, tailored to their duties, access levels and current cyber threats. The ISM also says training content should be tailored to groups such as general personnel and different classes of high-risk personnel.

sections.heading: What role-based advice does the ISM expect personnel to receive?

blocks.text: Beyond the annual course, several controls require specific groups to be advised about particular threats. These are best delivered as short targeted modules for the roles concerned, with the advice recorded.

items: **ISM-1740**: personnel dealing with banking details and payment requests are advised what business email compromise is and how to manage and report it.
**ISM-2071**: personnel dealing with user account details are advised what social engineering attacks are, how to manage them and how to report them.

**ISM-2126** (new in September 2026): personnel positively identify requestors using a pre-established authentication method or independent trusted channel before actioning requests to change account details, change banking details or conduct financial transactions. The ISM explains that AI now allows convincing synthetic voice and video impersonation.
**ISM-0817**: personnel are advised what suspicious contact via online services is and how to report it.

**ISM-0820, ISM-2104, ISM-2105, ISM-2106**: personnel are advised not to post work-related information, clearance and briefing details on unauthorised online services, to limit posting about their duties and skills, and to report cases where such information is posted.
**ISM-2074**: a general-purpose AI usage policy is developed, implemented and maintained, which training should explain alongside the web usage policy (ISM-0258).

blocks.title: What changed in the September 2026 release
blocks.text: ASD's [September 2026 changes document](https://www.cyber.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-08/ISM%20September%202026%20changes%20%28September%202026%29.pdf) records ISM-2126 on synthetic impersonation as a new control in the Guidelines for personnel security. ISM-1565 was among controls amended without changing their intent.

sections.heading: How do you turn the ISM controls into a training program?

blocks.text: Treat each control as a learning obligation with an audience, a frequency and an evidence requirement. The table below is an illustrative design, not ASD guidance.

States who the security contacts are and reports a suspected compromise through the right channel
Annual scenario assessment result per person
ISM-1565, privileged users, annually
Applies privileged access rules, such as using separate privileged and unprivileged operating environments (ISM-1380)

ISM-1740, finance and payments staff
Recognises business email compromise warning signs and follows the verification procedure
Scenario items based on real invoice and bank change requests

blocks.text: For the design steps, see [how to design a compliance training program](/guides/how-to-design-a-compliance-training-program) and [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles).

sections.heading: What evidence will an assessor look for?

blocks.text: An assessor will expect a register that proves annual completion by all personnel and privileged users, and content that covers the topics ISM-0252 names. Because ISM-2022 requires the register itself, a missing or incomplete register is a finding in its own right.

items: Training register (ISM-2022) listing every person, the modules required for their role, completion dates and content versions.
Content outline showing the five ISM-0252 topics are covered.
A list of privileged users drawn from access management, reconciled to ISM-1565 completions.
Records that role-based advice (ISM-1740, ISM-2071, ISM-2126) reached the relevant teams.
CISO oversight records, such as program approval and periodic reporting (ISM-0735).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records ISM controls as sources with their revision and update dates, and links each to the concepts, audiences and assessment points that depend on it. When ASD releases a new ISM version, changed controls can be traced to the content that needs review.

faqs.q: Is ISM awareness training mandatory for private companies?
faqs.a: Not by law. The ISM is a framework organisations apply through their own risk management. It is mandatory for non-corporate Commonwealth entities through the PSPF, and suppliers are often contractually bound to it. Private organisations commonly adopt it, or the Essential Eight, as a baseline.

faqs.q: How often does the ISM require awareness training?
faqs.a: ISM-0252 requires cyber security awareness training annually for all personnel, and ISM-1565 requires tailored privileged user training annually for everyone with privileged access. Role-based advice, such as on business email compromise, has no stated frequency, so it is usually delivered at role assignment and refreshed annually.

faqs.q: How often is the ISM updated?
faqs.a: ASD updates the ISM several times a year and publishes a changes document with each release. Control records show the month and year of each control's last update, for example Sep-26 for controls changed in the September 2026 release, which helps training owners find what has moved.

faqs.q: Does the ISM cover AI in awareness training?
faqs.a: Yes, in two ways. ISM-2074 requires a general-purpose AI usage policy, which staff need to understand, and ISM-2126 responds to AI-enabled synthetic voice and video impersonation by requiring independent verification before actioning account or payment changes.
